story.title: Tiger Woods Enters Plea Deal for Reckless Driving Charge Following Florida Crash
story.summary: Tiger Woods has pleaded no contest to a reckless driving charge related to a rollover crash in Florida earlier this year. As part of a plea agreement, he will face a five-year driving ban and a $1,000 fine. The incident reportedly occurred while Woods was distracted by his phone and adjusting the radio.

event_overview.title: About Tiger Woods Incident
event_overview.subject: Tiger Woods Incident
event_overview.summary: This event concerns the criminal case arising from Tiger Woods’ March 27, 2026 rollover crash on Jupiter Island in Martin County, Florida. Authorities initially alleged DUI-related offenses; the case was later resolved in Martin County court through an amended reckless-driving disposition rather than a trial on the original DUI allegation.

facts.label: Incident date and location
facts.value: The crash occurred on March 27, 2026, on Jupiter Island in Martin County, Florida, after Woods’ Land Rover collided with a trailer and rolled onto its side.

facts.label: Initial allegations
facts.value: Woods initially faced misdemeanor allegations of driving under the influence with property damage and refusing to submit to a lawful test; he entered a not-guilty plea before the case was amended.

facts.label: Court resolution
facts.value: On September 2, 2026, Woods pleaded no contest to an amended reckless-driving charge in Martin County, resolving the criminal case without a trial on the original DUI charge.

facts.label: Driving privilege consequence
facts.value: The court ordered a five-year driver-license suspension as part of the disposition. Separately, Florida law authorizes administrative license suspension when a driver refuses a lawful breath, blood, or urine test; that administrative process is distinct from the criminal case outcome.

facts.label: Court and records access
facts.value: The case was handled in Martin County, whose Clerk of Court maintains court-record access and processes public-records requests for records in its custody.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the September 2, 2026 plea-related developments, not the complete crash investigation, evidentiary record, medical-treatment history, or every prior driving-related incident involving Woods.

explore_lenses.label: Why did prosecutors accept a reduced charge?
explore_lenses.title: Evidence concerns shaped the plea
explore_lenses.summary: The plea replaced the original DUI accusation with reckless driving and a separate refusal-to-test disposition. The state attorney said the available evidence did not meet the proof standard for a controlled-substance DUI case.

claims.text: Woods had originally pleaded not guilty to DUI; on September 2 he entered no-contest pleas to reckless driving and refusal to submit to testing after the March rollover crash.

Martin County State Attorney Thomas Bakkedahl said toxicologists retained by both sides found insufficient proof that Woods was impaired, despite police reports, video, and pharmacy records being reviewed.
The reported facts included a negative breath test and a refusal to provide a urine sample; the refusal remained a separate charge in the agreement.

explore_lenses.label: How did the case reach this point?
explore_lenses.title: A crash, records fight, then a plea change
explore_lenses.summary: The case developed from a March 27 crash on Jupiter Island into a DUI prosecution that involved access to medical and prescription records before the parties reached a deal.

claims.text: Authorities said Woods' Land Rover clipped a truck and rolled onto its side; neither Woods nor the other driver was reported injured.
According to the arrest report, Woods told a deputy he had been looking at his phone and changing the radio station before the collision.

In July, Judge Darren Steele approved an agreement allowing prosecutors to seek hospital records and earlier approved access to pharmacy records, subject to a protective order requested by Woods' attorney.
Bakkedahl said the prosecution viewed the refusal charge as provable but considered a DUI trial uncertain because of the impairment evidence.

explore_lenses.label: What does the plea mean going forward?
explore_lenses.title: The driving penalty is the immediate consequence
explore_lenses.summary: The court imposed a five-year license suspension, while the no-contest plea is treated as a conviction in the criminal system even though it is not an admission of guilt. Florida law also provides a separate administrative framework for suspensions connected to test refusals.

claims.text: The judge ordered a five-year driver's-license suspension after Woods agreed to the reduced reckless-driving charge; AP reported that he also pleaded no contest to refusing testing.
A no-contest plea does not admit guilt, but it is treated as a conviction by the criminal justice system.
Under Florida law, a test-refusal suspension may be reviewed administratively, and the statute says the outcome of a related criminal case does not affect that administrative suspension.

story_report.summary: Tiger Woods pleaded no contest to reckless driving and refusal to submit to testing after a March rollover crash in Florida, resolving a case in which he had originally pleaded not guilty to DUI. A judge imposed a five-year driver’s-license suspension and a $1,000 fine under the agreement. The crash occurred after Woods’ Land Rover clipped a truck and rolled onto its side; no injuries were reported.

sections.heading: Crash Account and Investigation
sections.body: According to the arrest report, Woods told a deputy he had been looking at his phone and changing the radio station before the collision. Authorities said his Land Rover clipped a truck and rolled onto its side. Earlier in the case, a judge allowed prosecutors to seek hospital records and had approved access to pharmacy records, subject to a protective order requested by Woods’ attorney.

sections.heading: Prosecutors Cited Impairment Evidence
sections.body: Martin County State Attorney Thomas Bakkedahl said toxicologists retained by both sides found insufficient evidence to prove Woods was impaired after reviewing police reports, video and pharmacy records. Reporting described a negative breath test and Woods’ refusal to provide a urine sample; the refusal remained a separate charge in the plea agreement. Bakkedahl said prosecutors considered the refusal charge provable but regarded a DUI trial as uncertain because of the evidence on impairment.

sections.heading: Plea and License Consequences
sections.body: A no-contest plea does not admit guilt, but the criminal justice system treats it as a conviction. Florida law provides for administrative review of a suspension tied to a test refusal and says the related criminal case’s outcome does not affect that administrative suspension. The court’s five-year suspension followed Woods’ agreement to the reduced reckless-driving charge.

unresolved.text: Public reporting does not include the full plea agreement or the underlying expert reports, leaving the precise evidentiary assessment unavailable for independent evaluation.

The available reports do not state when the five-year court-ordered suspension begins or ends, whether a separate administrative suspension remains active, or whether Woods will seek review or restricted-driving privileges.

related_stories.summary: Richard Ravalomanana, the former Senate president of Madagascar, has been sentenced to 10 years of hard labor after being found guilty of complicity in murder related to a violent crackdown on youth-led protests last year. The unrest resulted in at least 22 fatalities and over 100 injuries, as reported by the UN.

related_stories.title: USS Abraham Lincoln Arrives in Thailand After Extended Deployment
related_stories.summary: The USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier has arrived in eastern Thailand after more than nine months at sea, primarily spent in the Middle East. Reports have emerged regarding challenging conditions on board, including food shortages and plumbing issues, prompting calls from some lawmakers for an investigation into the deployment's impact on crew welfare.
